Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

Title: Business Affairs Director

Role Summary

Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is seeking an experienced Business Affairs Director to serve as a senior commercial leader and lead some of our most significant, complex and strategically important negotiations for PlayStation Productions, our in-house production team focused on bringing PlayStation’s iconic game franchises to new audiences through film, television and other entertainment formats.

This is a senior individual contributor role requiring deep entertainment industry expertise, exceptional commercial judgment and the credibility to independently represent SIE in negotiations with senior executives across studios, streaming platforms, production companies, agencies, producers and other rights holders.

The Business Affairs Director will own commercial strategy and negotiation for material transactions from initial deal structuring through agreement on key business terms. The role will also advise senior leadership on deal strategy, commercial models, market precedent, risk and the longer-term implications of proposed arrangements.

Working in close partnership with Creative, Finance, Legal and our first-party game studios, the Business Affairs Director will determine and advocate for commercial positions that enable compelling creative partnerships while protecting and maximizing the long-term value and flexibility of SIE’s intellectual property.

This role does not have direct people management responsibility but is expected to operate as a senior leader through expertise, influence, judgment and functional leadership. This role is based in Culver City, CA.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead SIE’s most complex, material and strategically significant commercial negotiations across film, television and other entertainment projects, including development, production, licensing, co-production, and other strategic content arrangements.
• Set and drive commercial strategy for assigned transactions, establishing negotiating positions, identifying value drivers and acceptable trade-offs, and determining the appropriate path to successful outcomes.
• Independently negotiate with senior external counterparties, including studios, streaming platforms, production companies, producers, agencies, talent representatives and other rights holders, representing SIE’s interests with credibility and authority.
• Structure and negotiate key business terms across a range of entertainment agreements, including writer, producer, director, talent, attachment, option/purchase, licensing, co-production and related deals.
• Serve as a senior advisor to leadership on business affairs matters, providing clear recommendations on deal structures, commercial models, negotiation strategy, market precedent, business risk and long-term implications.
• Evaluate when established market or SIE precedent should be followed, challenged or evolved, balancing the requirements of individual projects with the potential implications for future transactions.
• Partner with Finance to understand project economics, valuations, value drivers and financial guardrails, translating those inputs into commercial strategy, deal structures and negotiating positions.
• Partner closely with Legal to ensure negotiated commercial positions are appropriately reflected in agreements, providing clear business direction and resolving commercial issues that arise through long-form negotiations.
• Work closely with our first-party game studios and IP creators to understand franchise priorities, rights considerations and long-term strategic objectives, ensuring deal structures appropriately protect and enhance the value of our IP.
• Identify and develop creative solutions to complex or novel commercial issues, balancing creative ambition, partner objectives, economics, risk and SIE’s long-term interests.
• Assess the broader implications of significant deal terms and structures across the PlayStation Productions portfolio, identifying potential precedent, opportunities and risks beyond an individual transaction.
• Build and maintain senior relationships across the entertainment ecosystem, including studios, platforms, agencies, producers, representatives and other strategic partners.
• Maintain a sophisticated understanding of entertainment industry economics, market practices, competitive dynamics, emerging business models and evolving deal structures, using those insights to inform SIE’s commercial positions.
• Provide subject matter leadership and expertise across PlayStation Productions and the broader organization, serving as a trusted resource on entertainment deal-making and business affairs matters.
• Drive cross-functional alignment on deals, synthesizing perspectives from relevant internal stakeholders and escalating material commercial decisions where appropriate.

Qualifications & Experience

• 10 to 15 years of progressive experience in entertainment business affairs, deal-making or a closely related commercial role, ideally within a major studio, streaming platform, television network, production company, agency or other sophisticated entertainment organization.
• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience required. JD, MBA or other relevant advanced degrees are preferred but not required.
• Extensive experience independently leading complex, high-value and strategically significant entertainment transactions, with a demonstrated track record of successful negotiations with senior executives and sophisticated counterparties.
• Deep expertise in entertainment industry business models, economics, deal structures, customs and practices across film and television.
• Strong working knowledge of intellectual property, licensing, development, production and distribution arrangements and their commercial implications.
• Demonstrated ability to develop commercial and negotiation strategy, evaluate deal economics and value drivers, and structure solutions to complex or novel business issues.
• Exceptional negotiation skills and commercial judgment, including the ability to assess leverage, determine appropriate trade-offs, navigate impasses and recognize when individual deal terms may create broader precedent.
• Demonstrated ability to operate with significant independence, authority and discretion, including in high-stakes or sensitive negotiations involving senior internal and external stakeholders.
• Strong executive presence, with the ability to establish credibility and effectively influence executives and counterparties at all levels of seniority.
• Ability to provide clear, pragmatic recommendations to senior leadership, distilling complex commercial issues into actionable choices and articulating the implications of different paths.
• Demonstrated ability to influence across functions and organizations without relying on reporting-line authority.
• Strong strategic thinking and creative problem-solving skills, particularly when navigating ambiguity, novel business models or precedent-setting transactions.
• Ability to manage multiple sophisticated negotiations and priorities simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
• Experience working with video game intellectual property, franchise-based entertainment or adaptations is a plus.

Please note that the base pay range may vary in line with our hybrid working policy and individual base pay will be determined based on job-related factors which may include knowledge, skills, experience, and location.

In addition, this role is eligible for SIE’s top-tier benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, matching 401(k), paid time off, wellness program and coveted employee discounts for Sony products. This role also may be eligible for a bonus package. Click here to learn more.

This is a flexible role that can be remote, with varying pay ranges based on geographic location. For example, if you are based out of Seattle, the estimated base pay range for this role is listed below.

$217,000—$325,000 USD

Job Description:

Growth Marketing Manager, New Games

Location: Stockholm, Sweden (On-site)
Craft: Marketing
Employment type: Full time

Build the growth engine for King’s next hit

New Games is where King explores what is next: new game ideas, new player experiences and new ways to grow. We are looking for a Growth Marketing Manager to sit at the heart of one of our New Games teams and help turn early concepts into games players want to discover, try and keep playing.

This is not a traditional, campaign-led marketing role. You will be an embedded, hands-on growth partner from the earliest stages of development - working alongside Product, Design, Engineering, Analytics and Creative to make smarter bets, test them quickly and learn faster.

You will bring a growth-hacker mindset: spot an opportunity, form a sharp hypothesis, build the test, read the signals and decide what happens next. Some experiments will not work. That is part of the job. What matters is the quality and speed of the learning, and how you turn it into a better game and a stronger route to market.

This is a high-autonomy individual-contributor role for someone who enjoys doing, not delegating. You will be broad across marketing, comfortable picking up work wherever it is needed, and excited to use AI tools to increase the pace and quality of your output. One week you might shape a player proposition, the next launch a creative test, interrogate funnel data or streamline how the team learns from experiments.

If you want to help build a game from concept - and get meaningful marketing tests into market within weeks - this could be your next move.

Your role within the Kingdom

As Growth Marketing Manager, New Games, you will:

• Embed in a cross-functional game team and influence product, player and growth decisions from concept through launch.
• Identify the biggest growth questions early, turn them into focused hypotheses and run rapid tests to answer them.
• Design and execute marketing experiments across propositions, audiences, channels, creative, store presence and early-player journeys.
• Bring performance marketing thinking into product development, connecting acquisition, conversion, retention and player value to product choices.
• Use player research, market signals, competitor analysis and data to uncover opportunities - and make clear recommendations.
• Partner closely with Product, Analytics, Creative, Development and central King teams to align on priorities, unlock expertise and move work forward.
• Build practical test-and-learn processes that make the team faster, clearer and more effective over time.
• Roll up your sleeves across the marketing mix: briefing creative developing positioning, analysing results, writing test plans and communicating the story behind the data.
• Use AI tools thoughtfully and responsibly to accelerate research, ideation, analysis, production and operational work.
• Communicate decisions and learning clearly to a wide range of stakeholders, creating alignment without slowing momentum.

What you will bring

Experience and mindset

• Experience in growth, performance, product, brand or consumer marketing within games, entertainment, apps or another digital consumer business.
• A demonstrable bias for action: you can take an ambiguous problem, create a plan and deliver a useful first version quickly.
• A test-and-learn mentality. You are comfortable taking smart risks, learning from setbacks and changing course when the evidence says to.
• Strong commercial and analytical instincts, with the ability to turn data into practical next steps.
• Comfort working in a fast-moving, start-up-like environment where priorities evolve and there is no large support team behind every task.
• Confidence collaborating across disciplines and influencing stakeholders with different perspectives.
• Hands-on experience with AI tools, or strong curiosity and evidence that you actively use them to improve how you work.

Games and player understanding

• Genuine curiosity about casual games and the people who play them.
• A clear point of view on casual games marketing: what is working, what is broken and what you would test differently.
• If you have not worked extensively in casual games, you can show that you understand the category, its players and the distinct challenges of marketing it.
• Curiosity about culture, entertainment and emerging player behavior - not just established marketing playbooks.

Who you are

You are likely someone who:

• Loves the blank page and the momentum of building something new.
• Moves quickly without losing sight of the player or the commercial objective.
• Enjoys wearing many hats and does not wait for a specialist team to make progress.
• Can be strategic and highly practical in the same day.
• Challenges assumptions constructively and brings others with you.
• Sees process improvement as a growth lever, not an administrative exercise.
• Gets energy from close, on-site collaboration with a game team.

Why New Games at King?

You will have the freedom and proximity of a small, ambitious game team, paired with the reach, craft and player understanding of King. Your work will shape real product decisions early when insight, creativity and a great experiment can have an outsized impact.

Come help us make the next generation of King games impossible to ignore.

About King

With a mission of Making the World Playful, King is a leading interactive entertainment company for the mobile world. For more than 20 years, we have created iconic games including Candy Crush and Farm Heroes Saga. King is part of Microsoft, with Kingsters based in Stockholm, Malmö, London, Barcelona, Berlin, Dublin, San Francisco, New York, Los Angeles and Malta.

About King

With a mission of Making the World Playful, King is a leading interactive entertainment company for the mobile world with more than 20 years of history of delivering some of the world’s most iconic games in the mobile gaming industry, including the world-famous Candy Crush franchise, as well as other mobile titles such as Farm Heroes Saga. Around 200 million people play a King game every month. King, part of Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), has Kingsters in Stockholm, Malmö, London, Barcelona, Berlin, Dublin, San Francisco, New York, Los Angeles and Malta. More information can be found at King.com or by following us on LinkedIn and @lifeatking on Instagram.

With 5,400+ employees and over 80,000 institutional, commercial, and payments clients, we operate from more than 80 offices spread across six continents. As a Fortune 100, Nasdaq-listed provider, we connect clients to the global markets – focusing on innovation, human connection, and providing world-class products and services to all types of investors.

Whether you want to forge a career connecting our retail clients to potential trading opportunities, or ingrain yourself in the world of institutional investing, StoneX Group is made up of four business segments that offer endless potential for progression and growth.

Business Segment Overview - Payments: A Swift-accredited service bureau and member, our Payments division provides NGOs, institutions and non-profits the ability to make a local difference, globally – with transparent pricing across 180+ countries and 140+ currencies.

Position Purpose: This role sits within the LATAM engineering group, working on mission-critical systems: order routing and trade capture, exchange and clearinghouse integrations (B3, CME, local CSDs), post-trade processing, regulatory reporting, and client-facing platforms. You will be a senior individual contributor with strong ownership over design and delivery, partnering directly with trading, operations, compliance, and global engineering teams.

Responsibilities

Design, build, and operate scalable, resilient, low-latency-tolerant systems that support StoneX's LATAM business lines. The role exists to raise the engineering bar on regional platforms, improving reliability, reducing manual operational load, and delivering the integrations and features required by local market structure and regulation, while aligning to StoneX global architecture standards.

Primary duties will include:

• Design and implement backend services and APIs supporting trading, clearing, settlement, and reporting workflows for LATAM markets.
• Own features end to end: requirements refinement with business stakeholders, technical design, implementation, testing, deployment, and production support.
• Build and maintain integrations with exchanges, clearinghouses, market data providers, and internal global platforms (FIX, REST, messaging, file-based protocols).
• Develop data pipelines and reconciliation processes feeding regulatory and internal reporting (CVM/B3, CNBV, and equivalents).
• Contribute to architecture decisions and technical documentation (ADRs, runbooks, integration specs); evaluate trade-offs on build vs. buy and global vs. regional solutions.
• Improve observability, automated testing, and CI/CD maturity across owned services; reduce toil through automation.
• Participate in code reviews and set standards for code quality, security, and performance within the team.
• Support incident response for production systems, including root-cause analysis and preventive follow-up.
• Mentor mid-level and junior engineers; act as technical reference for a domain or set of services.
• Coordinate with distributed teams across the US, UK, and Asia; including working across time zones and in English.
• This list of duties and responsibilities is not intended to be all-inclusive and can be expanded to include other duties or responsibilities that management deems necessary.

Qualifications

To land this role you will need:

• Professional software engineering experience, with demonstrated senior-level ownership of production systems.
• Strong proficiency in at least one of: C#/.NET, Java, or Python; solid working knowledge of a second language.
• Solid grounding in SQL and relational databases (SQL Server, PostgreSQL, or Oracle), including query tuning and data modeling.
• Experience designing and consuming APIs and integrating distributed systems; familiarity with messaging/streaming (Kafka, RabbitMQ, MQ) and event-driven patterns.
• Cloud experience (AWS or Azure) and containerization (Docker, Kubernetes).
• Practical experience with CI/CD, version control (Git), automated testing, and monitoring/observability tooling.
• Professional working proficiency in English (written and spoken); fluent Portuguese and/or Spanish.
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred

• Financial services or capital markets background, brokerage, clearing, asset management, exchange, or fintech.
• Domain knowledge of trading lifecycle, post-trade operations, market data, or risk; familiarity with FIX protocol.
• Exposure to LATAM market structure and regulation: B3, CVM, ANBIMA, SELIC/CETIP, CNBV, or local payments/settlement rails.
• Experience with regulatory or financial reporting pipelines and data reconciliation at scale.
• Infrastructure-as-code (Terraform), and performance/latency-sensitive system design.
• Experience working in a global matrixed organization with offshore/nearshore delivery models.

Working environment:

• Salary to be determined by the education, experience, knowledge, skills and abilities of the applicant, internal equity and alignment with market data.
• Full time (Monday to Friday), with an indefinite contract.
• Hybrid setting: 4 days in-office and 1 day from home.

Notice to Recruitment Agencies: Please be advised that any résumé or CV submitted to us without: (i) prior onboarding with StoneX as an approved recruitment partner; and (ii) prior written authorization/instruction from StoneX’s Talent Acquisition Team, will be treated as an unsolicited and unapproved submission. We may, at our discretion, review and consider such candidates; however, no placement fee, referral fee, or any other form of compensation will be payable to the submitting agency if the candidate is subsequently hired, and regardless of the agency’s involvement. Submission of a résumé/CV in these circumstances will be deemed acceptance of these terms, and these terms supersede any the agency seeks to impose on StoneX.
